name: PatchCamelyon (PCam): Histopathology Patch Classification Benchmark
description: PatchCamelyon (PCam) is a widely utilized benchmark dataset designed for machine learning research in digital histopathology without the compute overhead of gigapixel whole-slide processing. Derived from the CAMELYON16 sentinel lymph node dataset, PCam consists of 327,680 color image patches (96x96 pixels at 10x equivalent magnification) split into standardized training (262,144), validation (32,768), and testing (32,768) sets. A patch is labeled positive (binary 1) if its central 32x32 pixel region contains at least one pixel of tumor tissue, while excluding ambiguous borderline cases. PCam is balanced across classes and serves as an accessible testbed for rotation equivariance, self-supervised learning, and convolutional neural network development.
